This file combines the response variable, Democracy in 2020, with the 10 predictors for Mini Project 3. Five predictors are from Mini Projects 1 and 2 and five are new. Missing values are kept for now.

## Libraries

```{r}
#| label: libraries
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Loading Data

```{r}
#| label: import
#| message: false
# Predictors from Mini Projects 1 and 2
children   <- read_csv("../data/predictors/children_per_woman_total_fertility.csv")
co2        <- read_csv("../data/predictors/co2_pcap_cons.csv")
income     <- read_csv("../data/predictors/ilevels4_wb.csv", col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
sanitation <- read_csv("../data/predictors/at_least_basic_sanitation_overall_access_percent.csv")
poverty    <- read_csv("../data/predictors/number_of_people_in_poverty.csv")

# New predictors
employment <- read_csv("../data/predictors/aged_15plus_employment_rate_percent.csv")
energy     <- read_csv("../data/predictors/energy_use_per_person.csv")
inflation  <- read_csv("../data/predictors/inflation_annual_percent.csv")
lifeexp    <- read_csv("../data/predictors/lex.csv")
murder     <- read_csv("../data/predictors/murder_total_deaths.csv")

# Response
democracy  <- read_csv("../data/response/democracy2020.csv")
```

## Cleaning Data

Each file has one column per year. The function below drops the years after 2022 and pivots to one row per country and year.

```{r}
#| label: drop-and-pivot
drop_and_pivot <- function(df, value_name) {
  df |>
    select(-any_of(as.character(2023:2100))) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -c(geo, name),
      names_to = "year",
      values_to = value_name
    ) |>
    mutate(year = as.integer(year))
}

children_long   <- drop_and_pivot(children, "children_per_woman")
co2_long        <- drop_and_pivot(co2, "co2_per_capita")
income_long     <- drop_and_pivot(income, "income_level")
sanitation_long <- drop_and_pivot(sanitation, "sanitation_access_pct")
poverty_long    <- drop_and_pivot(poverty, "people_in_poverty")
employment_long <- drop_and_pivot(employment, "employment_rate_pct")
energy_long     <- drop_and_pivot(energy, "energy_use_per_person")
inflation_long  <- drop_and_pivot(inflation, "inflation_pct")
lifeexp_long    <- drop_and_pivot(lifeexp, "life_expectancy")
murder_long     <- drop_and_pivot(murder, "murder_deaths")
```

## Joining Data

All predictors are joined by country and year, then filtered to 2020 and joined with Democracy. Countries with no Democracy value are dropped, and nothing else is dropped.

```{r}
#| label: join
joined <- list(
  children_long, co2_long, income_long, sanitation_long, poverty_long,
  employment_long, energy_long, inflation_long, lifeexp_long, murder_long
) |>
  reduce(full_join, by = c("geo", "name", "year")) |>
  filter(year == 2020) |>
  arrange(geo, year)

combined <- joined |>
  inner_join(democracy, by = c("geo", "name"))
```

## Logging Variables

Counts and amounts that are very right skewed are logged. These are people in poverty, murder deaths, energy use per person and CO2 per capita. Inflation is not logged because 48 countries have negative inflation in 2020, and the log of a negative number does not exist. The rest are not strongly skewed.

```{r}
#| label: log-variables
combined <- combined |>
  mutate(
    log_people_in_poverty   = log(people_in_poverty),
    log_murder_deaths       = log(murder_deaths),
    log_energy_use          = log(energy_use_per_person),
    log_co2_per_capita      = log(co2_per_capita)
  ) |>
  select(-people_in_poverty, -murder_deaths, -energy_use_per_person, -co2_per_capita)
```

## Checking Data

```{r}
#| label: missing-check
dim(combined)
table(combined$Democracy)

# Missing values per column
colSums(is.na(combined))
```

## Writing Data

```{r}
#| label: write-data
write_csv(combined, "../data/combined_data.csv")
```
